raw.details:
MyOnne National Bug Bounty Challenge 2026

48 Hours. One Mission. Find What We Missed.

MyOnne is opening its application to India's security research community.

We invite independent security researchers, ethical hackers, penetration testers, application security professionals and cybersecurity students from across India to participate in the MyOnne National Bug Bounty Challenge 2026.

A 48-hour, nationwide online security research competition where participants will test the MyOnne application in an authorised testing environment, identify security vulnerabilities and responsibly report their findings.

Some vulnerabilities are worth discovering. Some discoveries deserve a bounty.

Event at A Glance

  • Event: MyOnne National Bug Bounty Challenge 2026
  • Total Bounty Pool: ₹3,00,000*
  • Duration: 48 Hours
  • Challenge Begins: thursday, 26 November 2026, 5:30 Pm Ist
  • Submissions Close: saturday, 28 November 2026, 5:30 Pm Ist
  • Format: fully Online – India-Wide
  • Participation: individual or Teams of 1–4 Members
  • Organiser: My Onne Amora Private Limited

Competition Platform & Execution

The My Onne National Bug Bounty Challenge 2026 Will Be Conducted Entirely Online Through My Onne's Security Research Platform, Which Is Developed and operated by My Onne Amora Private Limited.

The Competition Will Use My Onne's Dedicated Security Research Infrastructure for Authorised Application Testing and Vulnerability Reporting.

The Platform Consists Of:

  • Testing Environment: My Onne Security Research Platform, Providing Registered and Eligible Participants Access to the designated testing application, researcher credentials, and Android Ap Ks.
  • Vulnerability Reporting: Participants must submit all vulnerability reports, supporting evidence, and research findings through the Designated My Onne Security Research Platform.
  • Researcher Access: Testing Access and Application Packages Will Be Distributed Exclusively to Registered and Eligible Participants.

The Competition Will Be Conducted Within the Officially Authorised Testing Environment and Scope.

Who Can Participate?

The Challenge Is Open to Individuals and Teams from Across India, Including:

  • Independent Security Researchers and Bug Bounty Hunters.
  • Ethical Hackers and Penetration Testers.
  • Application Security Professionals.
  • Cybersecurity Students and Enthusiasts.
  • University Cybersecurity Clubs and Research Groups.

Participants Can Compete Individually or Form Teams of Up to Four Members.

Whether You Are an Independent Researcher or Part of A Cybersecurity Team, This Is an Opportunity to Demonstrate Your Skills Against a Real-World Application.

Testing Access & Application Handover

Registered and Eligible Participants Will Receive the Following Approximately 10–20 Minutes Before the Official Challenge Begins:

  • My Onne's Designated Testing Application.
  • Researcher Access Credentials.
  • Android Ap Ks Required for The Authorised Testing Environment.
  • Official Testing Scope and Rules of Engagement.
  • Testing Guidelines and Vulnerability Reporting Instructions.

This Advance Handover Allows Participants to Prepare Their Testing Environments Before the Official Competition Begins.

Important: Security testing must begin only within the Authorised Scope and according to the Official Challenge Instructions.

How the Challenge Works

The Competition Follows a Structured Research and Reporting Process:

Step 1 – Register

Register for The My Onne National Bug Bounty Challenge 2026.

Step 2 – Receive Testing Access

Eligible Participants Receive the Designated Application, Researcher Credentials and Android Ap Ks Before the Challenge Begins.

Step 3 – Review the Scope

Understand the Authorised Testing Scope, Rules of Engagement and Reporting Guidelines.

Step 4 – Discover Vulnerabilities

Conduct Security Research and Identify Potential Vulnerabilities Within the Authorised Testing Environment.

Step 5 – Submit Your Findings

Report Discovered Vulnerabilities with Supporting Evidence Through the Designated My Onne Security Research Platform.

Step 6 – Validation & Recognition

Submitted Reports Undergo Validation and Triage. Eligible Findings Are Considered for Bounty Rewards and Recognition in Accordance with The Official Programme Rules.

Responsible Disclosure & Important Rules

All Participants Must Follow Responsible Security Research Practices.

  • Testing Is Permitted only Within the Officially Authorised Scope.
  • All Discovered Vulnerabilities Must Be Reported Responsibly Through the Designated Reporting Channel.
  • Accessing, Modifying, Extracting or Disclosing Other Users' Data Is Strictly Prohibited.
  • Destructive Testing, Denial-Of-Service Attacks and Activities Outside the Authorised Scope Are Prohibited.
  • Duplicate, Invalid and Out-Of-Scope Reports May Not Qualify for Rewards.
  • Participants Must Follow All Official Testing Guidelines and Rules of Engagement.
  • Final Severity Classification, Report Validity and Bounty Eligibility Will Be Determined Through the Official Validation Process.

The Complete Authorised Scope, Reporting Instructions and Programme Rules Will Be Communicated to Eligible Participants Before Testing Begins.

prizes.others: Bug bounty pool of up to ₹3,00,000.  Rewards will be determined based on the number of valid, unique vulnerabilities reported, their severity, impact and successful validation by the MyOnne security team.  There is no fixed cash prize for the 1st-ranked team. Bounty payouts are based on the quality and severity of accepted findings, not leaderboard position alone.  The total payout is subject to the programme's scope, eligibility and validation rules.
